title: Regular sequences and short exact sequences
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $0\to M_1\xrightarrow{\alpha}M_2\xrightarrow{\beta}M_3\to0$ a short exact sequence of $R$-modules and $f_1,\dots,f_r\in R$. For $0\le i\le r$ write $I_i=(f_1,\dots,f_i)\subset R$. (a) Suppose that for every $i=1,\dots,r$ the element $f_i$ is a nonzerodivisor on $M_1/I_{i-1}M_1$ and on $M_3/I_{i-1}M_3$ (condition (1) of [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence] for $M_1$ and for $M_3$). Then for every $i=1,\dots,r$ the element $f_i$ is a nonzerodivisor on $M_2/I_{i-1}M_2$, and for every $0\le i\le r$ the sequence $0\to M_1/I_iM_1\to M_2/I_iM_2\to M_3/I_iM_3\to0$ induced by $\alpha,\beta$ is exact. (b) Consequently, if $f_1,\dots,f_r$ is an $M_1$-regular sequence and an $M_3$-regular sequence [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence], then it is an $M_2$-regular sequence.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0F1T (lemma-regular-sequence-short-exact-sequence), with its proof (snake lemma, Tag 07JW, and induction on r); part (a) is what that proof establishes, part (b) is the statement of the tag.
